mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly reduces the risk-free rate, increasing the present value of equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is linear: for every 1% decrease in FEDFUNDS, the 20-day forward return increases by 0.5% on average.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical inverse relationship between FEDFUNDS and equity returns
failure_condition: The Rank IC of FEDFUNDS against 20-day forward returns is less than 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window from 2008-11-15 onward.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:2008 Fed rate cut cycle (current rate 4.83, condition not met)
failure_condition: The win rate (percentage of positive 20-day returns) when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% is greater than 40%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5% and industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, it indicates a severe economic slowdown that triggers risk-off sentiment, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:2008 recession indicators (UNRATE=3.4, condition not met)
failure_condition: The win rate (percentage of positive 20-day returns) when UNRATE > 4.5 AND INDPRO < 100 is greater than 60%.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation that forces the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:2008 inflation concerns (CPIAUCSL=302.918, YoY change computable)
failure_condition: The win rate (percentage of positive 60-day returns) when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.5% is greater than 50%.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. The relationship is positive: for every 100-unit increase in HOUST, the 5-day forward return increases by 0.2% on average.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical positive correlation between housing starts and equity returns
failure_condition: The Rank IC of HOUST against 5-day forward returns is less than 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1200, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:2008 housing market decline (current HOUST=1420.0, condition not met)
failure_condition: The win rate (percentage of positive 20-day returns) when HOUST < 1200 is greater than 40%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising industrial production (INDPRO > 100) and falling housing starts (HOUST < 1400) signals a decelerating housing market that increases recession risk, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:2008 industrial and housing data (INDPRO=103.0258, HOUST=1420.0)
failure_condition: The win rate (percentage of positive 20-day returns) when INDPRO > 100 AND HOUST < 1400 is greater than 60%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.0% and the year-over-year growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) is below 0.5%, it indicates a weak labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:2008 labor market weakness (UNRATE=3.4, condition not met)
failure_condition: The win rate (percentage of positive 60-day returns) when UNRATE > 4.0 AND PAYEMS YoY growth < 0.5% is greater than 50%.
